audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant', final primary stress (rule 01 / 101, compounds excluded) rests on the 2021 ANU reference grammar, the best available and instrumentally supported description; the deciding quotation was verified verbatim at sec. 6.4.1 p. 241 with the schemata at sec. 5.5.4 p. 207 in the PDF downloaded this reading. The grammar itself disposes of the only competing claims (Simon 1979 and Blench draft on tone). No better source exists; nothing to add beyond registering the now-copies we hold and page numbers (207, 241) in the record and setting an strength of the evidence (record 'grade' field is empty; second reader had 'typeset-pdf').

sources.citation: Weedall 2021, A grammar of West Kameng Sajolang (Miji), ANU PhD, secs. 5.5.4 and 6.4 read from full thesis text; compounds excluded (stress by lexeme headedness), realized as pitch accent, no tone
sources.quote: Two-syllable words which are not compounds always have an initial unstressed syllable and a final stressed syllable. Three-syllable words which are not compounds always have an initial secondarily stressed syllable, a penultimate unstressed syllable, and a final primarily stressed syllable.
